newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Commission refuses to make statement on U.S. rice.
newsitem.headline: Commission refuses to make statement on U.S. rice.

text.p: The European Commission refused to make a statement to cereals experts on Thursday on the progress of its revision of a controversial regulation covering U.S. rice quotas to be allowed into the European Union under a GATT minimum access agreement, an EU official said on Tuesday.
"The Commission withdrew the proposal at the meeting of the cereals and rice management committee two weeks ago because it was clear that it would get a negative vote," the official said.
At this week's meeting of the committee "The Commission was asked what was happening and refused to say anything," the official said.
The agreement has been fiercely opposed by the European rice trade for allowing the U.S. government to place management of their quota arrangements in the hands of trade organisations.
"The whole thing has been a mistake from the beginning. The U.S. government saw our negotiators coming and the result is a blank cheque for fraudsters," a trade source told Reuters.
The European Rice Association, the EU umbrella organisation for rice traders, has been campaigning against the arrangements on the grounds that they would also lead to cross-subsidisation problems.

"The way the U.S. is proposing to allocate quotas would lead to problems of subsidisation. The European Rice Association has been campaigning for an end to the proposal and compensation under article 28 of the GATT agreement," a member told Reuters.
There was no discussion on any other matters at the meeting on Thursday, the official added.
